facts.statement: Serendipaceratops is a genus of herbivorous ornithischian dinosaur from the early Cretaceous of Australia that may be an ankylosaur.
facts.quote: Serendipaceratops (meaning "serendipitous horned face") is a genus of herbivorous ornithischian dinosaur, possibly an ankylosaur, from the early Cretaceous Period of Australia.

facts.statement: The first bone of Serendipaceratops, an ulna, was discovered in 1993 near Kilcunda on the south-east coast of Victoria, Australia.
facts.quote: The first known bone from Serendipaceratops, an ulna (lower arm bone), was in 1993 discovered in Australia near Kilcunda, on the south-east coast of Victoria.

facts.statement: The specific name arthurcclarkei honors science fiction writer Arthur C. Clarke.
facts.quote: The specific name honours science fiction writer Arthur C. Clarke.

facts.statement: The preserved length of the holotype ulna is about sixteen centimetres.
facts.quote: The holotype ulna has a preserved length of about sixteen centimetres.

facts.statement: The holotype dates to the early Aptian stage, approximately 115 million years ago.
facts.quote: Serendipaceratops is known only from its holotype NMV P186385, a single left ulna found in the Wonthaggi Formation, dating from the early Aptian, in 2003 considered to have been about 115 million years old.

facts.statement: A 2010 study suggested the ulna was more similar to the ankylosaur Minmi than to basal ceratopsians and lacked ceratopsian synapomorphies.
facts.quote: In a comprehensive survey of the dinosaurs from Australia and New Zealand, Federico Angolin and colleagues in 2010 found that the ulna did not especially resemble that of a basal ceratopsian any more than of any other quadruped genasaurian ornithischian, lacking ceratopsian synapomorphies, and that in fact it was more generally similar to the ulna of the Australian ankylosaur Minmi.

facts.statement: A 2021 study classified Serendipaceratops as an ankylosaur due to the robust proportions of its deformed ulna.
facts.quote: Most recently, Rozadilla et al. in 2021 found that while the taxon was valid, the ulna of Serendipaceratops was deformed, making Rich et al's conclusions about its classification invalid. Instead, Rozadilla et al. classified Serendipaceratops as an ankylosaur, because of the ulna's robust proportions.

facts.statement: A 2014 study argued the taxon is valid based on ulna proportions falling within ceratopsian morphospace.
facts.quote: However, in 2014 Rich et al. published a statistical study showing that the proportions of the holotype ulna fell within ceratopsian morphospace and found the taxon to be valid based on a unique combination of characters.

facts.statement: The fossil was found during the Dinosaur Cove project at the base of a cliff face near the coastline.
facts.quote: El hallazgo tomó lugar durante el proyecto "Dinosaur Cove", descubriéndose los restos en la base de la cara de un acantilado enfrente de la línea costera.

facts.statement: The fossil was excavated in the "Arch", a small area of sea floor protected from waves by a dam.
facts.quote: El fósil fue excavado en el "Arco", una pequeña área de suelo marino protegido de las olas por un dique.

facts.statement: Serendipaceratops lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 116 million years ago in the Aptian stage, in what is now Australia.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 116 millones de años, en el Aptiense, en lo que es hoy Australia.

facts.statement: The holotype ulna is about 16 centimetres long, has a broken olecranon process at the rear top, and a flattened shaft.
facts.quote: El cúbito holotipo tiene una longitud conservada de unos 16 centímetros. En la parte superior trasera, su proceso de olécranon se ha roto. El eje está bastante aplanado.

facts.statement: The discoverers initially did not consider the fossil might be ceratopsian, as they did not expect to find evidence of that group in Australia.
facts.quote: Inicialmente, los descubridores, Rich y Vickers-Rich, no habían considerado la posibilidad que podía haber sido un ceratopsiano siendo esta la última de las familias de dinosaurios que esperaban encontrar evidencia en Australia.

facts.statement: The discoverers initially tried to convince themselves the bone belonged to a theropod.
facts.quote: En su lugar habían intentado convencerse de que era el hueso de un terópodo.

facts.statement: Colleague Dale Russell later pointed out the ulna's striking similarity to that of the primitive ceratopsian Leptoceratops.
facts.quote: Algunos meses más adelante, sin embargo, en una visita al Museo Tyrrell de la paleontología en Alberta, Canadá, su colega Dale Russell les señaló su llamativa semejanza al cúbito del ceratopsio primitivo Leptoceratops.

facts.statement: It was originally described as a member of Neoceratopsia and one of the earliest known ceratopsians, possibly the only one known from the southern hemisphere.
facts.quote: Serendipaceratops fue descrito originalmente como un miembro de Neoceratopsia y uno de los primeros dinosaurios ceratopsios conocidos, y el único conocido en el hemisferio sur, con la posible excepción de Notoceratops, un género suramericano dudoso, que también puede ser de otro tipo de dinosaurio ornitisquio.

facts.statement: Another supposed ceratopsian ulna was found in the Eumeralla Formation in south-west Victoria, dating to 106 million years ago.
facts.quote: Además del holotipo, se encontró otro supuesto cúbito ceratopsiano en Dinosaur Cove, en el suroeste de Victoria. Es un poco más joven con 106 millones de años, habiéndose encontrado en la Formación Eumeralla.

facts.statement: A study by Angolin et al. found the ulna lacked ceratopsian synapomorphies and was more generally similar to the ankylosaur Minmi.
facts.quote: En un estudio sobre de los restos de dinosaurios de Australia y Nueva Zelanda, Federico Angolin y colaboradores encontraron que el cúbito no tenía ningún parecido particular a los ceratopsianos basales, no más del que tendría cualquier otro ornitisquio genasaurio, careciendo de sinapomorfias propias de los ceratopsios, y que de hecho se parecía más en términos generales al cúbito del anquilosaurio australiano Minmi paravertebrata.

facts.statement: The genus Serendipaceratops was named by Rich and Vickers-Rich in 2003.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Serendipaceratops (genus), Rich and Vickers-Rich 2003

facts.statement: Serendipaceratops belongs to the parent group Ceratopsia.
facts.quote: Parent group: Ceratopsia

facts.statement: Serendipaceratops is classified within the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Serendipaceratops is Serendipaceratops arthurcclarkei.
facts.quote: Type species: Serendipaceratops arthurcclarkei

facts.statement: Serendipaceratops lived during the Aptian stage, from 121.4 to 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 119.57 million years ago)

facts.statement: Only one fossil occurrence of Serendipaceratops has been recorded.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1
